title: Errors, logging, retries, HTTP clients, redaction, observability
tldr: Failures become strings at every boundary and are re-parsed: one typed classifier (FailoverReason) plus 9+ substring classifiers with 5 vocabularies (ERR-01, ERR-02, ERR-12).
Biggest kill: ~1,800 first-party import guards and 379 wrappers around config reads that already fail open (ERR-11); the in-tree Langfuse plugin (ERR-10); unused tenacity core dep (ERR-03).
Biggest simplification: one event bus; shared metrics is fed by the hook bus AND 110 direct imports in 69 core files, beside a separate monitoring emitter and the Relay coordinator (ERR-09).
Low-hanging (S/M, high): 7 — ERR-01, ERR-02, ERR-03, ERR-04, ERR-05, ERR-07, ERR-12.

One logging pipeline (mostly) and one provider error model; no shared retry policy (~95 loops), no shared HTTP client outside provider calls (4 stacks, 3 proxy policies), one redaction engine with ~10 failure policies.

SQLite error predicates and persistence-error classes
second failure vocabulary for bot-mode retries (regex over text)
build_keepalive_http_client: the only shared HTTP client (provider SDK calls)
Nous opt-in shared-metrics telemetry: store, sender, Relay subscriber, consent
gateway/cron health events, own emitter queue + thread, OTLP export

findings.title: Failures are flattened to strings and re-classified by 9+ substring classifiers with 5 vocabularies
findings.problem: The provider path has a typed model (FailoverReason + ClassifiedError with recovery hints). It is lost at the first boundary: error_surface writes reason.value into a dict key and later code parses text again. tools/bot_failure_reasons.py keeps a second 14-code vocabulary and regex-classifies error + failure_reason text even when the typed reason is in the same dict (:119). classify_cron_error and classify_gateway_error are two more substring tables with their own labels; the gateway rule _contains_any('auth','token',...) labels any message containing 'token' as auth_failed. 30+ hand-written _is_transient_/_is_retryable_/_looks_like_ predicates do the same per module. Every new provider or platform error string means editing several drifting tables, and a wrong classification decides whether a turn is re-run.
findings.move: Create agent/failure.py with a frozen Failure value type (kind: FailureKind = FailoverReason extended with disk_full, network, delivery_timeout, cancelled, runtime_offline, missing_config; retryable; retry_after; resets_at; message; to_dict/from_dict). Turn results carry result['failure'] instead of five loose keys; child processes print one 'HERMES_FAILURE {json}' stderr line. retry_action, error_surface, cron_health and gateway_health become dict[FailureKind, X] lookups; the three text classifiers merge into one legacy-text fallback in agent/failure.py.

reference.pattern: retry_context(on=...): retry policy keyed on a typed exception/predicate, never on text

findings.risk: Bot relay, desktop error cards and cron incident labels change if a mapping is wrong. Preserve the RETRY_* decision for every existing reason, failure_resets_at card text (#98852), billing/free-tier surfaces.

findings.title: Gateway send retry decides 'retryable' by OR-ing four signals, two of them substring parses; error_kind is ignored
findings.problem: The adapter holds the typed exception at its except, writes str(exc) into SendResult.error and only sometimes sets retryable=True or error_kind. _send_with_retry re-derives the decision from error.lower() substrings on every attempt; adapters override _is_retryable_error with more substrings (Photon matches the literal text 'retryable=false'). 55 adapter sites set retryable=True or override the predicate. A library that rewords its exception changes retry behaviour silently; the never-retry-timeouts rule is a substring check.
findings.move: Route every failure through SendResult.failed(exc, *, kind=None, retry_after=None), which runs classify_send_error once on the exception object at the adapter's except site and stores error_kind. _send_with_retry branches only on error_kind and retry_after. Delete SendResult.retryable, _is_retryable_error, _is_rate_limited_error, _is_timeout_error and the per-adapter overrides.
findings.risk: Per-platform retry semantics (Photon sidecar markers, Telegram FloodWait). Preserve: no retry on timeouts, 60 s inline-wait cap (#91969), no notice inside a flood penalty, partial-delivery resume.

findings.title: No retry primitive: ~95 hand-rolled retry loops, a 174-line backoff helper, and tenacity pinned in core with zero importers
findings.problem: scripts/err_retry_loops.py finds 210 for/while loops with a try plus a sleep/backoff call or an attempt counter (plugins 50, gateway 48, hermes_cli 41, tools 31, root 16, agent 11, pm 7). A seeded sample of 22 had 10 real retry loops, so ~95 exist, each with its own attempts, delay curve, jitter, exception set and logging. Only 9 call agent.retry_utils.jittered_backoff. tenacity==9.1.4 is a pinned core dependency with no in-scope importer. Tests need an autouse stub to zero jittered_backoff (pyproject.toml:858); loops that sleep directly cannot be stubbed.
findings.move: Adopt stamina (a thin layer over the already-shipped tenacity): for attempt in stamina.retry_context(on=pred, attempts=N, timeout=T), with typed on= predicates from ERR-01/ERR-02/hermes_state_errors.is_sqlite_lock_error. stamina.set_testing(True) replaces the autouse stub. Keep parse_retry_after_seconds and reset parsing; delete jittered_backoff. If stamina is rejected, drop tenacity from core dependencies.

reference.pattern: retry_context with typed on=, attempts, timeout; set_testing in src/stamina/_config.py:174

findings.risk: Retry timing users see (Telegram reconnect, SQLite busy). Preserve: server Retry-After beats backoff, inline wait caps, KeyboardInterrupt/CancelledError never retried, agent-loop credential rotation stays in the loop.

findings.title: One redaction engine, ~10 failure policies: 16 guarded call sites, two fail open, and 42 force=True egress calls bypass redact_for_egress
findings.problem: redact_sensitive_text takes five boolean modes. redact_for_egress calls itself the one scrub for text leaving the process and fails closed, but has 4 callers while 42 sites pass force=True directly and skip its bearer sweep. 16 sites wrap 'from agent.redact import' in try/except Exception, each with its own fallback sentinel; two return the raw input: the Langfuse exporter (external service) and cron incidents (disk). tools/mcp_tool_common.py keeps a private credential regex, send_message_senders adds two more, monitoring and support redaction each add an e-mail regex, and debug_redaction imports private names from agent.redact. Gist: 145 secret_leak_redaction fix commits.
findings.move: Replace the flags with redact(text, purpose) where Purpose = MODEL|FILE_READ|TERMINAL|LOG|DISK|EGRESS|EXPORT|SUPPORT; one table row per purpose (passes, mask style, whether the user toggle applies). The function fails closed itself. Delete the 16 try-wrappers, the MCP regex, the send_message extras and the two PII copies.

reference.pattern: configure(processors=...): one ordered processor chain per output instead of flags at each call

findings.risk: Over-redaction of tool output if a purpose maps to the wrong passes (#35519, #43025, #34029). Map each current flag combination to exactly one purpose before deleting flags.

findings.title: The log session tag is a threading.local that is never cleared and never reaches tool worker threads
findings.problem: 'hermes logs --session' filters by the [session] tag, which comes from a threading.local set at turn start. clear_session_context has zero callers, so a pooled executor thread keeps tagging unrelated records with the previous session. Parallel tool workers get ContextVars copied but not the threading.local, so tool log lines carry no tag. Compression needed explicit rebind calls to paper over it. gateway/session_context.py already binds HERMES_SESSION_ID as a ContextVar that every thread hop copies.
findings.move: Move the session ContextVars from gateway/ into a neutral leaf module (hermes_context.py) importable by hermes_logging; the record factory reads it. Delete set_session_context, clear_session_context, _session_context and the three call sites.

reference.pattern: merge_contextvars: log context read from ContextVars at emit time

findings.risk: CLI and cron paths that never call set_session_vars must still bind the id. Preserve 'hermes logs --session' matching and HERMES_SESSION_ID subprocess env semantics.

findings.title: Multiplex log routing is built into the handler stack because formatting was moved off the caller's thread
findings.problem: _NonFormattingQueueHandler skips the stdlib prepare() that formats on the emitting thread, so formatting and redaction run on the listener thread where the profile scope is gone. That forces a per-record uncached get_hermes_home().resolve() on the caller, a second per-record resolve plus 2 s liveness probes in _ProfileRoutingFileHandler, per-record set_hermes_home_override re-binding, and _redact_enabled reading .env/config.yaml from the listener thread. About 400 of 980 lines are routing and queue lifecycle.
findings.move: Format and redact on the emitting thread (stdlib QueueHandler.prepare) and stamp record.hermes_home_key = hermes_home_key() (cached). The listener routes pre-rendered strings to files[key]. Delete the override re-binding, the listener-thread policy fallback and the per-record resolves.

reference.pattern: QueueHandler.prepare formats on the producer thread; see also structlog src/structlog/stdlib.py:1012

findings.risk: Redaction CPU moves to caller threads (measure). Preserve deleted-profile release (#103777, Windows lock files), managed 0660 perms, external-rotation reopen.

findings.title: tool_calls.log is a second, unqueued file-logging pipeline that writes every profile's tool calls into the launch profile's log
findings.problem: With display.tool_progress: log the gateway writes tool calls through its own stdlib RotatingFileHandler on gateway.run._hermes_home, which is get_process_hermes_home() captured at import. Under multiplex a secondary profile's tool calls land in the launch profile's tool_calls.log (profile-scope leak class, 366 fix commits). It bypasses the queue (writes on the asyncio loop), the Windows rollover lock (#44873), managed perms and profile routing, and polls a queue every 0.3 s per turn.
findings.move: Add a tool_calls.log row to setup_logging's handler_specs with a component filter on 'hermes.tool_calls', exclude that logger from agent.log, and log directly from the producer. Delete _tool_call_logger, _tool_call_logger_lock, _run_agent_write_tool_log and the per-turn log_queue.

reference.pattern: one QueueListener consumer thread for all file handlers

findings.risk: Keep the '%(message)s' line format; agent.log must not double the lines; keep redaction.

findings.title: Network policy is decided per call site: 4 HTTP stacks, 101 client constructors, 3 proxy policies
findings.problem: 33 httpx.Client, 36 httpx.AsyncClient, 29 aiohttp.ClientSession, 2 requests.Session constructions plus 41 httpx, 23 requests and 49 urlopen one-shots (scripts/err_http_ast.py); files importing httpx 86, aiohttp 34, requests 25, urllib.request 6. Only provider SDK calls share a client, and it deliberately ignores the macOS system proxy; gateway adapters shell out to scutil --proxy and use it; MCP has a third resolver; ~200 other sites get library defaults. Behind a corporate proxy each subsystem behaves differently. Clients built inside retry loops redo the TLS handshake per attempt.
findings.move: One hermes_platform/net.py owning NetPolicy (proxy-for-URL with one NO_PROXY matcher, CA/verify, default httpx.Timeout/Limits, user agent) resolved per profile; http_client(purpose)/async_http_client(purpose) return long-lived httpx clients with event hooks for redacted debug logging. Migrate requests and urlopen sites; ban new requests/urllib.request imports outside the module via TID251. aiohttp only where an SDK requires it.

reference.pattern: Timeout and Limits (:159) as typed objects; event_hooks on a long-lived client (httpx/_client.py:199)

findings.risk: Proxy behaviour changes for setups that work by accident; pick the policy once and document it. Preserve provider transport pooling, Codex happy-eyeballs, Telegram SOCKS, url_safety SSRF checks.

findings.title: Telemetry is fed by two mechanisms and 110 direct imports from core into hermes_cli.observability; three in-process event pipelines coexist
findings.problem: Shared metrics is Nous's opt-in usage telemetry (consent module; posts to telemetry.nousresearch.com). It receives lifecycle events as a privileged first-party observer ahead of plugins in hermes_cli/lifecycle.py, and is also called directly: 110 import lines in 69 files (agent 15, tools 9, gateway 10, tui_gateway 6, cron 3, acp 2, hermes_cli 22, root 2) import record_*/observe_*/note_* from 15+ submodules; tool handlers run inside telemetry wrappers. agent/ and tools/ import hermes_cli for this. agent/monitoring/emitter.py runs its own queue and dispatcher thread, and agent/relay_runtime.py (1,440 lines) its own coordinator.
findings.move: One typed in-process event bus owned by agent/ (agent/events.py: frozen event dataclasses, emit() never raises, subscribers registered at startup). Core and tools only emit. Shared metrics, monitoring/OTLP and plugins subscribe. Move hermes_cli/observability/ to a top-level telemetry/ package that imports agent, never the reverse; the 110 direct imports become ~20 emit() calls at existing hook points.

reference.pattern: named signals with decoupled receivers; structlog _config.py:202 configure-once

findings.risk: Telemetry schema (hermes.metrics.event.v3) and consent gating must not change; scope ordering (model call vs task run); the opted-out hot path must stay free (relay_shared_metrics.py:1319).

findings.title: Kill the in-tree Langfuse plugin: a third-party product plugin that fails open on export redaction and configures via non-secret env vars
findings.problem: Root AGENTS.md:97-102 says observability backends do not land under plugins/; this one did (42cc905c13). Its redaction wrapper returns the raw value on failure for content exported to an external service. It is configured by non-secret HERMES_LANGFUSE_* env vars (BASE_URL, ENV, RELEASE, SAMPLE_RATE, MAX_CHARS, MAX_DEPTH, DEBUG, CAPTURE) against AGENTS.md:80-83, and core carries special cases for it. Gist 0-plan §5 lists it as an unsettled contradiction.
findings.move: Publish as a standalone plugin repo; delete plugins/observability/ and the two core touchpoints.
findings.risk: Users with plugins.enabled: [langfuse] lose traces until they install the external package; show a one-line notice in 'hermes plugins' for that id.

findings.title: Most broad excepts have two structural causes: first-party import guards and config reads that already fail open
findings.problem: All 8,052 broad handlers by shape (scripts/err_except_shapes.py): logs 2,839; silent 1,986; import-only try 1,429; other 933; re-raise 486; config read 379. 1,795 of 1,933 import-guard tries guard only first-party modules (scripts/err_import_guard.py), which can only fail on a broken install or a real bug. Config readers already fail open (config_read_errors.py:1-7), so the 379 wrappers catch AttributeError/TypeError from walking an untyped dict. Seeded sample of 40: 15 legitimate boundary, 9 should be narrow, 12 hide a bug (5 config reads, 3 first-party import guards), 4 log-and-continue. Gist: swallowed exceptions are the top static fix class (106 strict / 669 by diff shape).
findings.move: (1) Delete try/except Exception around first-party imports; a broken install fails at the entry point and 'hermes doctor' reports it. (2) Typed config accessors (CFG-02) remove the config-read wrappers. (3) Name the boundaries (tool handler, JSON-RPC method, platform callback, plugin hook, thread/task top) with one decorator each that logs with exc_info and converts to the boundary's error type; anywhere else needs a reason comment.

reference.pattern: ExceptionRenderer: render exceptions once at the boundary

findings.risk: A removed guard can crash a path that relied on it for an optional extra; keep the 138 third-party import guards narrowed to ImportError. Preserve plugin isolation at the plugin-hook boundary.

findings.title: JSON-RPC errors are 89 magic numbers reused across meanings; clients decide by regex on message text
findings.problem: _err(rid, code: int, msg) is called at 349 sites with 89 distinct integer literals; two have names. The TUI documents that 4001 is reused for unrelated refusals and matches message text, and decides whether to re-dispatch a slash command that may mutate state by regex on the 4018 message. A reworded backend string changes client control flow. Messages are raw str(e) sent to a possibly remote client without redaction.
findings.move: tui_gateway/errors.py with class RpcError(IntEnum), one member per meaning (split 4001/4018); _err(rid, RpcError.X, msg); the contract generator emits the TS enum into gateway-contract.generated.ts; clients branch on code only; _err redacts msg with Purpose.EGRESS (ERR-04).
findings.risk: Old clients matching current numbers: keep numeric values for unchanged meanings, add codes only for the split cases.

import cannot fail; each invents a failure policy, two fail open (ERR-04)
hide broken installs and real bugs (ERR-11)

ProcessorFormatter renders in the producer context

Timeout and Limits (:159) as typed objects

seam_answer: Logging: yes, mostly. hermes_logging.setup_logging feeds one queue and listener for every entry point; the exceptions are the gateway's tool_calls.log (ERR-07) and three basicConfig entry points without redaction (mcp_serve.py:713, hermes_cli/plugin_host_child.py:571, agent/transports/hermes_tools_mcp_server.py:140). The session context uses the wrong primitive (ERR-05) and multiplex routing costs ~400 lines (ERR-06). Error model: one good typed model for provider calls (FailoverReason), lost at the first boundary; 9+ string classifiers with 5 vocabularies do the rest (ERR-01, ERR-02, ERR-12); 308 custom exception classes with no common root, 113 subclassing RuntimeError directly. Retry policy: none; ~95 hand-rolled loops, a backoff helper used 9 times, and an unused tenacity (ERR-03). HTTP: one shared client for provider SDK calls; everything else builds its own across 4 stacks and 3 proxy policies (ERR-08). structlog's contextvars model would delete the threading.local session tag and its rebind calls, and its processor chain is the shape for redaction purposes; a wholesale structlog swap is not needed. stamina would delete ~95 loops, jittered_backoff and the test stub, on top of tenacity which already ships. A shared httpx client per purpose deletes three proxy resolvers and requests/urlopen on core paths. The observability package (10k lines) is Nous's own opt-in telemetry (consent, telemetry.nousresearch.com): first-party and gated, so it stays, but as a subscriber on one event bus outside hermes_cli rather than 110 imports from agent/tools/gateway (ERR-09). Langfuse is a third-party product and should leave the tree (ERR-10).

ERR-06 assumes producer-side formatting is cheap enough; no measurement; microbenchmark RedactingFormatter.format.
Whether any tui_gateway _err(rid, ..., str(e)) message can carry a secret today (ERR-12); audit exception sources for the 5095/5031 sites.
Whether removing requests from core breaks a transitive dependency user; verify with 'uv tree --invert --package requests' in a lab copy.
